title_en: Guiding Case No. 263: A Network Information Technology Co., Ltd. v. A Information Technology Co., Ltd. — dispute over unfair competition
ruling_gist_en: An online platform that provides linked account services to users, transfers data obtained by the user on the linked network platform after obtaining the user's authorization, and provides convenience for the user to process such data within a reasonable scope, does not constitute unfair competition if it does not disrupt the order of market competition.

full_text_en:
Guiding Case No. 263

A Network Information Technology Co., Ltd. v. A Information Technology Co., Ltd. — dispute over unfair competition

(Discussed and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, released on August 28, 2025)

Keywords civil/unfair competition/data/associated account services/user authorization

Ruling Gist

Where a network platform provides associated account services to users, and, upon user authorization, transfers data obtained by the user on an associated network platform, facilitating the user's reasonable processing of such data, and does not disrupt the market competition order, such conduct does not constitute unfair competition.

Basic Facts

A Network Information Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as A Network Company) operates Website A, which provides job opportunities and career development opportunities for job seekers. When filling out their resumes, individual members may set control permissions, either allowing recruitment enterprise users to search for resumes or prohibiting any person, including recruitment enterprise users, from searching. After recruitment enterprise users post job vacancies on Website A, job seekers may, through their individual member accounts, independently search for positions and proactively submit resumes to target positions. In addition, Website A also provides paid resume search services for recruitment enterprise users, i.e., after purchasing the service, recruitment enterprise users may enter the database of Website A to search for resumes that job seekers have permitted to be searched. The resumes obtained by recruitment enterprise users through the above two methods (receiving submissions and proactive searching) may be viewed, downloaded, or sent to a designated email address within the member account. Users are required to enter a CAPTCHA consisting of image characters to log in to Website A.

A Information Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as A Information Company) operates Website B, which primarily provides resume management, recruitment management, big data services, and the like. Website B has an "Associate External Account" function designed to facilitate recruitment enterprise users in centrally processing resumes obtained from Website A and other websites. Recruitment enterprise users are required to give specific authorization to use this function. By entering their account numbers and passwords from Website A and other websites, they can automatically log in to the associated website and can choose whether to synchronize and obtain resumes into the recruitment management process or resume database of Website B.

A Network Company discovered that personal resumes obtained by recruitment enterprise users on Website A through receiving submissions and proactive search downloads could be found on Website B after using the "Associate External Account" function. In response, A Information Company stated that after recruitment enterprise users use the "Associate External Account" function, resumes can only be synchronized into the recruitment enterprise user's own account on Website B, and other users cannot search for them in the aggregated resume database of Website B. Regarding the above situation, A Network Company and A Information Company respectively notarized the relevant evidence.

On November 23, 2017, A Network Company filed a lawsuit on the grounds of an unfair competition dispute, alleging that A Information Company's provision of associated account services, using recruitment enterprise user accounts and passwords, bypassing the identity verification code mechanism to automatically access the system of Website A, and obtaining, storing, and using the resumes involved in the case constituted unfair competition. It requested that A Information Company be ordered to cease the unfair competition acts, eliminate the impact, and pay economic damages of RMB 5,000,000.

Judgment

The Shanghai Yangpu District People's Court rendered a civil judgment (No. (2017) Hu 0110 Min Chu 25167) on May 17, 2019, dismissing all claims of A Network Company. After the judgment was announced, A Network Company appealed. The Shanghai Intellectual Property Court rendered a civil judgment (No. (2019) Hu 73 Min Zhong 263) on October 13, 2020, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

Reasoning

The dispute in this case focuses on whether the conduct of A Information Company in providing associated account services and obtaining, storing, and using the resumes involved in the case constitutes unfair competition.

First, associated account services are a relatively common service model in cyberspace. Specifically, associated account services achieve the sharing of data, permissions, or functions by binding a user's multiple accounts on different network platforms, thereby providing a more convenient user experience. For example, in the current online recruitment service market, there are many information publishing platforms. To obtain more talent resource information, recruitment enterprises generally register as enterprise users on multiple recruitment websites simultaneously. To facilitate recruitment enterprise users in managing such job-seeking information scattered across different platforms simultaneously, some operators use website association technology to aggregate data from different platforms, allowing recruitment enterprise users to associate with their original platform accounts through the operator's website and then aggregate information for "one-stop" processing. Another example is the widespread use of associated account functions in the field of email. Provided that data security, personal information, and social public interests are not harmed, it is a lawful and legitimate act for network users to use the associated account function to transfer data held by them between different network platforms.

Second, the conduct of A Information Company in providing associated account services is justified. A Network Company has made substantial investments and contributions to the data collected and generated by Website A and enjoys rights protected by law. However, it must not hinder recruitment enterprise users from reasonably processing the collected data, including transferring it. Accordingly, relevant recruitment enterprise users may transfer resume data collected through methods such as paying consideration or receiving submissions from job seekers, including transferring it using associated accounts. Moreover, the associated accounts involved in the case did not exceed job seekers' expectations regarding the scope of personal information processing. After recruitment enterprise users use the "Associate External Account" function, resumes can only be synchronized into the recruitment enterprise user's own account on Website B. Job seekers' information cannot be searched in the aggregated resume database of Website B, and there is no circumstance infringing upon the lawful rights and interests of job seekers.

Third, the conduct of A Information Company in obtaining, storing, and using resume data from Website A with user authorization does not constitute unfair competition. (1) The associated account service provided by A Information Company requires recruitment enterprise users to choose whether to associate, whether to automatically synchronize or save resumes, and to input their account numbers and passwords from Website A and other websites on their own. The realization of the associated account function service is entirely based on the user's own will and requires the user to perform the corresponding operations. (2) As verified by a technical investigation officer, the program set by A Information Company to read the CAPTCHA is a technical means used to realize the associated account function, allowing users to log in to the website after associating accounts without additional verification. This does not constitute "acts that hinder or disrupt the normal operation of network products or services lawfully provided by other business operators" as stipulated in the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China. (3) When recruitment enterprise users use the associated account service of Website B and choose to synchronize resumes, the resumes they obtained on Website A are downloaded to the server of Website B. This is an inevitable result of realizing the associated account function. At the same time, the resumes synchronized to Website B can only be searched and browsed within the recruitment enterprise user's account, and others cannot obtain them on Website B. Therefore, the acts of obtaining and storing data involved in the case also do not constitute unfair competition.

In conclusion, the acts of A Information Company involved in the case did not disrupt the market competition order, nor did they harm the lawful rights and interests of other business operators or consumers, and thus do not constitute unfair competition.

Relevant Legal Provision

Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China.
